# Scenix v1.7.0 — Particles

Scenix `1.7.0` adds the optional `scenix-particles` crate: deterministic CPU
particle systems with a `no_std`-capable core, plus an instanced billboard GPU
draw path and an optional GPU compute simulation in `scenix-renderer`.
Everything is additive and feature-gated; the default facade build behaves
exactly like v1.6.0.

## Highlights

- `scenix-particles` is a standalone, `no_std`-capable CPU crate (std/serde
  features): `ParticleEmitter` builder, pools up to `PARTICLE_POOL_LIMIT`
  (262,144), burst + rate spawning, per-particle `Particle` records
  (`position`, `velocity`, `age`, `lifetime`, `size`, `rotation`, `flipbook`
  frame), and one reusable `ParticleRenderBatch` per update.
- A module vocabulary composes behavior on the emitter: `Gravity`, `Drag`,
  `ColorOverLifetime` (deterministic `ColorCurve` keys with sRGB/linear aware
  blends), `SizeOverLifetime`, `SpinOverLife`, and `ConfineBox`, all behind
  the `ParticleModifier` trait. `EmissionShape` covers points, spheres,
  hemispheres, discs, cones, and boxes with a `toward` shortcut.
- Simulation is seeded, so identical configs replay identically across
  resets and hosts — verified by an integration test that re-runs the same
  scenario twice.
- `scenix-texture::FlipbookGrid` is the pure frame-index → UV math shared by
  particles and sprites (uniform `columns × rows` sheets, top-left origin,
  clamp-pad on the last frame). The particle side mirrors it with
  `FlipbookConfig` for frame rate and looping.
- `scenix-mesh::quad_geometry(width, height)` builds the CCW +Z billboard
  quad with scenix's plane UV convention (v = 1 at the bottom), usable for
  sprite and expanded-fallback draws.
- `scenix-material::ParticleMaterial` carries tint, optional sprite texture,
  optional flipbook, soft-edge fade, and an `Additive` VS `Alpha` blend enum.
  Its `FeatureBits` add `FEATURE_SOFT_PARTICLES` (`1 << 20`) and
  `FEATURE_FLIPBOOK` (`1 << 21`), and `ShaderKind::Particles` selects the
  billboard pipeline key.
- `scenix-renderer` (behind `renderer` + `particles`) owns a GPU particle
  registry: `register_particles` installs a slot, `update_particles` uploads
  one CPU batch per frame into an instanced buffer, `resolve` hooks into
  registered textures, and `encode_frame` draws camera-facing billboards from
  a 64-byte instance record (center/size, premultiplied color, UV rect,
  rotation). Additive and alpha pipelines share the depth-test-on /
  depth-write-off contract, so particles layer over the lit scene without
  sorting.
- Optional GPU compute: `register_particle_compute` seeds a 64-byte-per-slot
  GPU pool from a CPU system snapshot; `simulate_particles_compute` then
  integrate gravity + drag with size/color fades and dispatches a
  deterministic ring-window respawn pass (single invocation, no atomics).
  `read_particle_pool` / `read_particle_ring` copy results back to the host
  for editors, debugging, and tests.
- CPU updates always win: calling `update_particles` converts a slot back to
  the CPU-driven draw path.
- `scenix-wasm` documents the browser fallback plan: WebGPU gets the full
  draw + compute path, WebGL 2 gets instanced billboards with CPU
  simulation, and WebGL 1 expands billboards to real quad geometry.
- `scenix-shader` math gains a public `scenix_math::float` shim module
  (sqrt/sin/cos/tan, inverse trig, atan2, cbrt) so `libm`-only EfFn builds
  keep the same APIs as std builds.

## Small Example

```rust
use scenix::{
    ColorOverLifetime, ColorCurve, Drag, EmissionShape, FlipbookConfig, Gravity, ParticleEmitter,
    ParticleMaterial, ParticleSystem, Vec3, SizeOverLifetime,
};

let emitter = ParticleEmitter::new()
    .with_rate(240.0)
    .with_lifetime(0.9, 1.6)
    .with_size(0.2)
    .with_speed(4.0, 7.0)
    .at(Vec3::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    .toward(Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 0.0))
    .with_shape(EmissionShape::Cone { radius: 0.15, height: 0.35 })
    .with_modifier(Gravity::new(Vec3::new(0.0, -12.0, 0.0)))
    .with_modifier(Drag::new(0.15))
    .with_modifier(ColorOverLifetime::new(ColorCurve::from_to(
        [1.0, 0.85, 0.35, 1.0],
        [0.9, 0.15, 0.0, 0.0],
    )))
    .with_modifier(SizeOverLifetime::from_to(1.15, 0.05));

let mut system = ParticleSystem::new(emitter, 1_024, 2021018); // deterministic seed
system.set_flipbook(Some(FlipbookConfig::full(4, 4, 24.0)));
system.update(1.0 / 60.0); // advances the CPU sim and returns the render batch

// GPU: registration is one call; `Renderer::update_particles` uploads the
// batch as instanced billboards (renderer + particles features).
let material = ParticleMaterial::new()
    .with_color(scenix::Color::from_rgb(1.0, 0.9, 0.6));
```

## Feature Flags

- `particles`: enables `scenix-particles` through the facade with curated
  re-exports (emitters, modifiers, curves, batches, flipbook config) plus
  the default-enabled material/texture types the draw path needs.
- `particles` + `renderer`: the GPU billboard path and the optional compute
  simulation (`register_particles`, `update_particles`,
  `register_particle_compute`, `simulate_particles_compute`,
  `read_particle_pool`).
- `particles` + `wasm`: browser fallback plan helpers
  (`particle_fallback_plan`) published through the facade wasm surface.
- `scenix-particles` standalone: `no_std`-capable CPU crate (std/serde
  features).

## Examples

```sh
cargo run -p scenix --example particles_basic --features particles
# GPU tail (needs a wgpu adapter; lavapipe works):
cargo run -p scenix --example particles_basic --features particles,renderer
```

## Compatibility

- All 19 workspace crates are version `1.7.0` and require Rust `1.98`.
- No existing enum gained variants; default features are unchanged.
- `NodeKind::Particles { system_id }` joins the scene graph and reports as
  `"particles"` in inspector snapshots; scene YAML/JSON payloads that never
  wrote particle nodes are unaffected.
- The GPU pool record is 64 bytes (four `vec4` fields) and the draw instance
  is 64 bytes; both are re-exported as `PARTICLE_POOL_STRIDE` and
  `PARTICLE_INSTANCE_STRIDE` for direct consumers.
- GPU-gated tests (`SCENIX_RUN_GPU_TESTS=1`) cover the billboard pipeline
  against a headless renderer and the compute lifecycle (integrate → expire
  → ring respawn → cursor boundary) on lavapipe-friendly software
  platforms.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p scenix-particles --all-features` — CPU simulation determinism,
  capacity and spawn-burst behavior, modifier composition, flipbook batches,
  and serde round trips.
- `cargo test -p scenix --test scenix_v17 --all-features` — facade-level CPU
  coverage across particles, material bits, flipbook grids, billboard
  geometry, float shims, and browser fallback plans.
- `SCENIX_RUN_GPU_TESTS=1 cargo test -p scenix-renderer
  --test particles_gpu --features particles` — wgpu pipeline + compute
  validation on software rasterizers.
